claims.text: Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi has 20 at.% each of Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni.
The quinary CrMnFeCoNi alloy can have an FCC structure.
The quinary alloy and all relevant quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
The quinary alloy has superior yield strength and strain hardening relative to its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets.
Increasing constituent count from the ternary and quaternary subsets to CrMnFeCoNi increases local lattice distortion.
CrMnFeCoNi develops more short-range chemical order than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Local lattice distortion and short-range chemical order create a heterogeneous local energy landscape.
The heterogeneous local energy landscape impedes dislocation glide.
More effective impediment of dislocation motion promotes dynamic strain hardening.
The five-element alloy has larger atomic-size mismatches than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Reduced chemical complexity in the quaternary and ternary alloys lowers local heterogeneity and produces more homogeneous slip.
More homogeneous slip in the quaternary and ternary alloys causes earlier failure.
Under identical room-temperature, quasi-static conditions, CrMnFeCoNi will have higher yield strength than the quaternary and ternary subsets.
Under identical room-temperature, quasi-static conditions, CrMnFeCoNi will have a higher strain-hardening rate than the quaternary and ternary subsets.
Under identical room-temperature, quasi-static conditions, CrMnFeCoNi will have greater ductility and delayed necking relative to the quaternary and ternary subsets.
The deformation response and mechanisms of equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi can change with temperature.
The proposed constituent-count mechanism may not apply at strain rates outside the quasi-static regime.
The relative contributions of lattice distortion and short-range order to dislocation pinning are not quantitatively established.
TEM can characterize dislocation density and arrangement in the compared alloys.
Atom-probe tomography can conclusively assess both local lattice distortion and short-range chemical order in these alloys.
